groups.reason: Connectivity reflects bounded protocol transactions; refresh performs profile-declared reads without arbitrary address access.
Reads exactly one unsigned 16-bit holding register at a zero-based address; no writes or profile-derived scaling.

Creates typed entities for all four standard data areas on every supported transport. Profiles may reject exact raw sentinels, round to reviewed decimal precision, or explicitly clamp bounded reads; writes still reject sentinels, non-finite values, range violations, and excess precision. Compatible network streams batch safe contiguous ranges and reuse serialized connections; every write resolves only stable profile point IDs and enforces type, bounds, confirmation, and read-back. FC15 commands bind ordered contiguous writable coils and fixed reviewed values; steady commands are idempotent while pulse reset intents are durably journaled and reconciled after restart. Multi-register types use explicit byte and word ordering without executable format strings.

Reviewed profiles compose exact point IDs into semantic state roles and commands. Commands resolve one immutable writable point plus either a fixed profile value or one named argument; caller-supplied unit, address, function, and point overrides are ignored.

Each profile selects one explicit transport. TCP/TLS use persistent serialized streams, UDP uses bounded MBAP datagrams, RTU-over-TCP and serial RTU validate CRC framing, serial ASCII validates delimiters, hex and LRC, and server-authenticated TLS-wrapped Modbus/TCP requires a CA certificate with hostname validation and no cleartext downgrade. Every DNS result is revalidated as local before connection.

Profile-declared coils and discrete inputs expose typed quality-bearing entities through the profiled-point roles above. Named immutable coil commands use FC05 or FC15, require protocol confirmation and read-back, never expose caller-selected addresses, and never retry writes automatically.

Profile-defined type, width, byte/word order, scale, offset, unit, bounds, enum, bitfield, precision, invalid-vector and access metadata drive the quality-bearing values and named confirmed writes represented by the profiled-point roles above.

Demand-driven, not a generic Modbus release requirement. Derived rates belong in reviewed semantic profiles. FC07/08/11/12/17/20/21/22/23/24 require a documented device use case and bounded fixture before exposure; destructive diagnostics, vendor functions and arbitrary function selection remain excluded.

TCP uses persistent serialized connections and safe contiguous batching. Parent-owned poll groups support independent priority and cadence, interval zero, inter-message delay, bounded jitter and exponential failure backoff. Redacted diagnostics expose poll outcomes and latency, stale counts, retries, reconnects, timeout/CRC/error taxonomies, queue high-water marks, and per-unit success history; online, offline, degraded, recovered, stale, and recovered events emit once per transition rather than becoming broad automation actions.

The parent requires the compatible shared sidecar package; the sidecar has internal-only networking, production fail-closed authentication on every operational route, and accepts only stable /dev/serial/by-id paths while preventing duplicate ownership of one resolved physical bus.

State distinguishes service availability, port state and responsive units; exposes queue depth/capacity/high-water, timeout, CRC/LRC, transport and reconnect counters; and reconciles configuration after sidecar restart. Manual queue flushing and transport restart controls are intentionally omitted because bounded expiry and automatic recovery provide the safe operational path.
Unrestricted addresses, vendor function codes, raw frames, broad writes, unsafe diagnostics, secrets, and serial-device access must not be exposed.
